Geographic focus:
    Europe, Serbia (Deliblatska Pescara reserve, ~80km from Belgrade), with reference to Greece (West Peloponnese)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — references past fires (1996, 2007, 2023–2025) and the recent blaze
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — immediate decisions on debris removal, erosion risk, bark beetle risk
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — 15–25 year restoration horizon, 3–5 year observation period recommended, increasing wildfire frequency under climate change

Synopsis:
    Serbian foresters are developing a restoration plan for the Deliblatska Pescara sand dune reserve after a major wildfire. The core challenge is deciding what to replant given that historically dominant species (black pine, black locust) are fire-prone and climate change is making wildfires more frequent. Experts advocate a slow, cautious approach — years of damage assessment, gradual removal of burned material, and a 3–5 year observation window before large-scale replanting. The 2023–2025 period was Serbia's worst for wildfires this century, and parallels are drawn with post-fire reforestation challenges in Greece.
